rounds.text: Shri Bajrang Alliance Ltd trades at an exceptionally modest P/E ratio of 11.6x based on filed statements [E1], which drastically undercuts the broader sector benchmark P/E of 23.91x [E6]. This valuation disconnect is even more pronounced on a relative value basis using data provider metrics, where the company's P/B ratio sits at a minuscule 0.42x compared to a sector benchmark of 2.55x [E7]. Beyond cheap multiples, the underlying profitability metrics demonstrate strengthening operational efficiency, highlighted by a robust recent return on equity of 16.5% [E13] and a rising median ROE trajectory that reaches 16% over the last year [E29]. Furthermore, long-term wealth creation potential is underpinned by a solid 15% compounded sales growth rate over a 10-year horizon [E14] alongside a stellar 47.5% CAGR in profit growth over the past 5 years [E57]. Recent operational tailwinds confirm this positive trajectory, as profit growth exceeds one-year price growth by 224% [E55], supported by recent quarterly sales momentum [E68]. Conceded: [E16], [E17].

The business suffers from severe and accelerating top-line contraction, highlighted by a compounded sales growth rate of -20% over 3 years [E16] and an even worse -32% over the trailing twelve months [E17], alongside a quarterly sales decline of -41% YoY [E69]. This dismal top-line performance is part of a longer-term deceleration where 5-year compounded sales growth limps at just 5% [E15], severely lagging the sector median sales growth of 18.3% [E74]. Furthermore, capital efficiency remains lackluster, evidenced by a meagre Return on Assets (ROA) of 0.54%—vastly underperforming the sector benchmark of 4.93% [E8]—and a modest Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) of 8.9% [E12]. Shareholder returns are further undermined by a complete lack of cash return, with the dividend yield sitting flat at 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: the company has delivered good profit growth of 47.5% CAGR over the last 5 years [E57] and trades at a modest P/E ratio of 11.6x [E1].
